metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. signs with Browns practice squad
metadata.description: Jimmy Horn Jr. officially signed with the Browns' practice squad on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Horn opened the season with the Panthers, returning punts and kicks while also getting one target in the passing game during Week 1. The second-year pro out of Colorado fumbled a punt in the season-opening loss, which led to a Bears' field-goal. Horn was let go by the Panthers earlier this week and has joined his former college teammate Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn - Added to Browns' practice squad
metadata.description: The Browns signed Horn to the practice squad Thursday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
metadata.analysis: Horn was waived by the Panthers on Tuesday, so he will get another opportunity in Cleveland, albeit as a member of the practice squad. The 2025 No. 208 overall pick appeared in 14 regular-season games for Carolina since entering the league, amassing 11 catches (16 targets) for 108 yards and adding eight carries for 69 yards.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. expected to sign with Browns
metadata.description: Jimmy Horn Jr. is expected to sign a deal to join the Cleveland Browns.
metadata.analysis: Horn is expected to land a deal with the Browns after being cut by the Panthers earlier this week. He isn't expected to have any fantasy relevance on this subpar offense for the foreseeable future, but he could mix in the rotation and play a real role for this team throughout the course of the season.

metadata.title: Browns Expected To Sign Receiver Jimmy Horn Jr.
metadata.description: The Cleveland Browns are expected to sign former Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr., Jordan Schultz reports. The move will reunite Horn, a Colorado Buffaloes standout, with quarterback Shedeur Sanders, who also played at Colorado under his dad as head coach. In Horn's career, he recorded 11 catches on 16 targets for 108 yards with no touchdowns. He also added eight rushes for 69 yards with a fumble lost. Horn was drafted in 2025 in the sixth round of the NFL Draft with pick No. 208 by the Panthers. He joins the Browns, who have established receivers in Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Jerry Jeudy. Horn will join the practice squad in Cleveland and look to break in with the regular team.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn - Let go by Carolina
metadata.description: The Panthers waived Horn on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: The wide receiver played 14 offensive snaps in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Bears last Sunday. Horn was unable to catch his only target but did log 101 kick-return yards and 17 punt return yards over 12 special-teams snaps. The wide receiver will likely end up back with the Panthers on the practice squad if he can clear waivers.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. waived by Panthers
metadata.description: The Panthers waived WR Jimmy Horn Jr.
metadata.analysis: Horn did not see one target in Week 1. He will look to land a fresh start with another team.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. Waived by Panthers
metadata.description: The Carolina Panthers have waived wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr., per ESPN's Adam Schefter. A sixth-round pick out of Colorado in the 2025 NFL Draft, Horn Jr. recorded just 11 catches for 108 yards on 15 targets across 13 games as a rookie. His sophomore campaign got off to a rough start in Week 1, as he muffed a punt in Carolina's blowout loss to the Chicago Bears. Whether or not the special teams mistake is the direct reason for Horn Jr. losing his spot on the Panthers' roster, the 24-year-old will now be looking for his next NFL opportunity. Depending on where Horn Jr. ends up, he could still carry some deep-league dynasty intrigue. For now, he remains firmly off the radar of redraft managers.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. sees one target in Week 1
metadata.description: Jimmy Horn Jr. failed to catch his only target in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Horn Jr. was more of an afterthought in the Carolina passing attack in the season opener, finishing last on the team in targets. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn Jr. Falling Down Depth Chart with Teammate Healthy
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr. is slipping down the depth chart, which has also caused his fantasy stock to fall. A couple of weeks ago, it seemed like Horn might have a chance to compete for the No. 3 receiver role with Xavier Legette (ankle) sidelined. However, Legette is back to 100%, leaving no chance for Horn to start in Week 1. The 24-year-old will likely find himself in the No. 4 or 5 receiver role to open the season. He's coming off a quiet rookie campaign in which he caught 11 passes for 108 yards, ranking as the WR138 in PPR leagues. Although he now has a pro season under his belt, Horn still may not emerge as a top-100 fantasy receiver this year. He can be avoided in all redraft and most dynasty leagues.

metadata.title: Jimmy Horn - Only two touches in final exhibition game
metadata.description: Horn caught his only target for five yards and added six yards on his only carry during Friday's 16-13 preseason win over the Texans.
metadata.analysis: The 2025 sixth-round pick also returned two punts, but those gained just two yards. With Xavier Legette (ankle) getting hurt in practice this week, the Panthers' No. 3 receiver job could be open to begin the campaign, but Horn didn't exactly make a strong final case to claim it. Over 14 regular-season games as a rookie, Horn caught 11 of 15 targets for 108 yards and added 69 rushing yards on eight carries.
